Images for textured faces

Source: R/textures.R
texture_3d.Rd

Wraps an image so that surface layers can drape it over their faces and annotation_raster_3d() can lay it on a plane. Texture coordinates u (left to right) and v (bottom to top) run from 0 to 1 across the image, as in OpenGL and rgl; points outside the image take the face's fill, or nothing when the fill is NA. The image is painted over the fill, so a transparent image region shows the fill.

Usage

texture_3d(image, interpolate = TRUE, extent = NULL)

Arguments

image

A nativeRaster (such as png::readPNG(native = TRUE)), a raster or matrix of colours, a numeric matrix of grey levels or a numeric array of grey, grey and alpha, RGB or RGBA channels in [0, 1] (such as png::readPNG()), or the path of a PNG file (needs png). Row one is the top of the image.

interpolate

Whether to interpolate between pixels (bilinear and mipmapped sampling) or to show them as sharp squares, as grid::rasterGrob() does.

extent

NULL, or four numbers c(umin, umax, vmin, vmax): the range of the layer's texture coordinates that the image covers. A surface layer without explicit u and v uses its x and y positions (its parameters for stat_parametric_3d(), its texture coordinates for an rgl mesh), so an extent in data units places an orthophoto over a terrain. NULL stretches the image over the range of the layer's coordinates.

Value

A ggplot3d_texture object.

Details

The raster backend and the view_3d() viewer sample the image per sample, perspective-correctly, in linear light: bilinearly where the image is magnified and from a mipmap (Williams 1983) where it is minified. The vector backend draws unlit images once per face triangle through an affine group transformation clipped to the triangle (R >= 4.2 groups, Murrell 2021). Under an orthographic camera every triangle maps the image affinely, which is exact; under perspective, triangles are split until the affine map lies within half a device pixel of the projective one. Raster devices resample the image with their own filter, in encoded sRGB. svglite writes transformation matrices with two significant digits, which can misplace the image by about 1% of its size; ragg, pdf(), cairo_pdf() and svg() keep it in place. Lit faces use the shared texture sampler and linear-light shading kernel to build colour-correct multiply and screen layers in one clipped group per face run. The hybrid renderer handles devices with limited compositing support. Text and labels are drawn over the scene. view_3d() and glTF export (export_3d()) carry the image and the texture coordinates.

References

Williams (1983). Pyramidal parametrics. SIGGRAPH Computer Graphics 17(3), 1-11. doi:10.1145/964967.801126

Murrell (2021). Groups, compositing operators, and affine transformations in R graphics. Technical report, University of Auckland.

See also

annotation_raster_3d(), geom_raster_3d() and the texture argument of geom_surface_3d() and geom_mesh_3d().

Examples

checker <- matrix(c("black", "white"), 8, 8)
checker[] <- ifelse((row(checker) + col(checker)) %% 2 == 0, "black", "white")
tex <- texture_3d(checker, interpolate = FALSE)
tex
d <- expand.grid(x = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 21), y = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 21))
d$z <- with(d, exp(-2 * (x^2 + y^2)))
ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, y, z = z)) +
  geom_surface_3d(texture = tex, shade = FALSE) +
  coord_3d()
